stories.head: AAMP 2.3 forces CMOs to rethink compliance when AI agents make vendor decisions at machine speed
stories.plain: SafeGuard Privacy's Richy Glassberg explains how the new AAMP 2.3 standard changes the compliance game: AI media agents can now select and pay vendors faster than any human can review contracts. CMOs need automated privacy rails baked into agent workflows before regulators or partners catch them flat-footed. A concrete governance wake-up call for any team deploying agentic buying.

stories.head: GTM teams are losing visibility and ownership of their AI agents
stories.plain: As AI agents multiply across sales, marketing, and ops stacks, most teams have no central registry of what each agent does, who owns it, or when it acts. The piece outlines the risks — duplicated actions, conflicting decisions, compliance gaps — and argues that agent governance is now a GTM infrastructure problem, not just an IT one.

stories.head: ZoomInfo MCP connector gives Replit builders natural-language access to verified GTM data
stories.plain: ZoomInfo's Model Context Protocol connector is now live inside Replit's marketplace, letting developers query verified company and contact data in plain language with no custom API work. This lowers the barrier for teams building AI-powered GTM tools, and signals that MCP is becoming a real distribution layer for data providers wanting to reach AI-native builders.

stories.head: UserTesting MCP servers embed human-participant research directly inside AI build tools
stories.plain: UserTesting's two new MCP servers let teams recruit real participants and validate AI-generated ideas without leaving ChatGPT, Claude, or Figma Make. Tapping a 7-million-person panel across 34 countries from inside an AI workflow closes the loop between generation and human validation — a meaningful shift in how AI content gets tested before it ships.

stories.head: Stop treating LLMs like thinking partners — treat them like deterministic tools
stories.plain: The article argues that anthropomorphizing LLMs leads to vague prompts, hallucinations, and outputs you can't reliably reuse. Framing the model as a structured, rule-following tool — not a collaborator — produces more consistent marketing content. Practical advice for any marketer building repeatable AI workflows or handing prompts to non-technical colleagues.

stories.head: GTM teams are losing track of their AI agents
stories.plain: As AI agents spread across GTM stacks, most teams have no clear map of what each agent does, who owns it, or what decisions it makes. This matters because ungoverned agents create compliance risk and can act against each other or customers. It directly shapes how marketing AI is built and governed going forward.

stories.head: Iterable Fall Release adds native RCS, Nova Conversations, Integrations Hub, and new AI Agents
stories.plain: Iterable's biggest platform update yet bundles a native integrations hub, RCS messaging, AI-driven conversation agents, and a continuous learning loop across customer data. The breadth of changes — new channels, new agents, new data connectors — shows how engagement platforms are racing to become all-in-one agentic systems, which changes how buyers evaluate and consolidate martech.

stories.head: OpenAI testing third-party-style tracking in ChatGPT ads
stories.plain: OpenAI is trialling a persistent identifier for ad measurement inside ChatGPT, similar to third-party cookies. If adopted, it reshapes how marketers buy and measure ads inside AI assistants, and raises fresh consent and privacy governance questions at a moment when the ad industry is still adapting to cookieless standards.

stories.head: AAMP 2.3 forces CMOs to rethink compliance when AI agents make vendor decisions at machine speed
stories.plain: SafeGuard Privacy's Richy Glassberg explains how AAMP 2.3 raises the compliance bar for AI agents that pick media vendors autonomously — a task no human compliance officer can review in real time. It highlights a practical governance gap that will affect every team deploying agentic buying tools.

stories.head: Dataiku launches Agent Management to track and govern AI agents across any platform
stories.plain: Dataiku's new Agent Management layer discovers, measures value, and flags risk for agents regardless of where they were built — filling the visibility gap highlighted by the 'losing track' problem. It is one of the first enterprise tools focused specifically on cross-platform agent governance, signalling a new buying category forming in martech.

month.skicker: 30-day synthesis · the shape underneath the feed

themes.head: AI Agents Are Escaping Oversight
body: Go-to-market teams are deploying AI agents faster than they can track them, creating blind spots in accountability and performance. The problem is no longer adoption — it is governance at scale, as agents multiply across sales, marketing, and customer-journey functions without a central registry or audit trail.

Platforms like Dataiku are responding with dedicated agent-management layers, and MarTech advisors are calling for formal AI governance frameworks before the sprawl becomes unmanageable. The decision that changes here is whether to build agent infrastructure first or governance infrastructure first — and the evidence says governance must lead.

themes.head: Proprietary Data Is the Real Moat
body: Competitive advantage is shifting from which AI model a company uses to what proprietary knowledge that model is trained or grounded on. TransUnion's research frames this as the AI confidence-readiness paradox: organizations trust AI outputs but have not cleaned the data feeding them, making results unreliable at the moment they matter most.

This reframes data management from a back-office function to a strategic priority. Partnerships like Evalueserve-Databricks and product moves like Iterable's persistent customer memory are all bets on the same thesis: the brand that structures its institutional knowledge first will widen its AI lead over time.
ev: Agile Brand · TransUnion data readiness paradox

themes.head: AI Search Is Rewriting Discovery
body: AI-powered search is no longer a future scenario — it is actively redirecting purchase intent, and in some cases telling consumers not to buy a product at all. OpenAI testing third-party-style ad tracking inside ChatGPT signals that the AI interface layer is becoming a full commerce and advertising surface, not just an information utility.

B2B brands are countering generic AI-generated content ('AI slop') by investing in authentic creator video, which both resonates with human audiences and earns citations in AI search results. Marketers now face a two-front battle: optimise for AI retrieval while producing content human enough to be preferred when AI summarises the category.

MarTech · B2B creator video vs AI slop

themes.head: The CMO Role Is Being Redefined by Delegation
body: When AI assistants draft the answer, write the content, and run the campaign, the question becomes what senior marketers actually own. Klaviyo's Jamie Domenici argues CMOs retain judgment, brand voice, and accountability — but must actively defend that territory rather than assume it is safe.

MarTech's skills-survival analysis and the framing of AI as a 'marketing coworker' (Snappy AI for financial advisors, AI coworker team-building guides) both point to the same structural shift: marketing headcount decisions will hinge on which tasks humans do measurably better than agents, not on roles as traditionally defined.
ev: Agile Brand · Klaviyo CMO & AI delegation
MarTech · building a team with AI coworkers

themes.head: Creative AI Is Collapsing Toolchain Walls
body: Adobe embedding its creative suite inside Google Gemini and Claude, UserTesting injecting human-insight data directly into AI workflows via MCP servers, and ZoomInfo connecting GTM.AI natively to Replit — these moves share a single logic: AI capability is becoming a layer that sits across tools, not inside any one of them. The era of the isolated SaaS application is ending.

For buyers, this changes vendor evaluation fundamentally. The question is no longer 'which tool does this best?' but 'which platform's API & integration story will let our stack stay coherent as models evolve?' Integration platforms (Workato's Gartner recognition is a signal) and open protocol standards like MCP are becoming as strategically important as the AI models themselves.
ev: Agile Brand · Adobe in Gemini & Claude

month.takeaway: Across every layer of the stack — search, creative, data, agents, and org design — AI is forcing marketers to decide what only humans should own before the default answer becomes 'nothing.'
